title: How a Fingerprint Sensor Works in 60 Seconds 👆🔐 #shorts
description:
A phone fingerprint sensor doesn't take a photo of your finger. A grid of tiny capacitor plates feels where the ridges of your skin touch and where the valleys leave a gap, builds a map from it, and compares the key points with your saved print. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#fingerprint #smartphone #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Your phone reads your fingerprint with tiny *electric charges*, not a camera.

steps.label: Grid
steps.text: Under the button sits a grid of thousands of tiny *capacitor* plates.

steps.label: Ridges
steps.text: Skin conducts electricity. *Ridges* touch the plates, while *valleys* leave a tiny air gap.

steps.label: Map
steps.text: Each plate measures a different *charge*, building a map of ridges and valleys.

steps.label: Match
steps.text: The chip finds key points, like ridge *endings* and *splits*, and compares them with your saved print.

steps.label: Unlock
steps.text: If enough points match, the phone *unlocks* in a fraction of a second.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Touch, sense, *match*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
